high.title: Expert: VN-Index will soon reach 2,000 points
high.summary: The VN-Index has established a new historical peak at 1,925 points, surpassing the previous record of 1,918 points. However, market enthusiasm is not as widespread as in previous breakthrough sessions. Liquidity has not truly exploded, foreign investors continue net selling, while capital continuously rotates among large-cap groups. Experts note the market structure has changed significantly - after a prolonged hot streak, Vingroup stocks are showing signs of cooling while capital flows are spreading to other sectors, particularly banking with strong gains in VPB, VCB, BID, ACB, and TPB. Oil & gas stocks like GAS and BSR are also gaining momentum. For VND/bond traders, this shift suggests a broadening market rally that could support sustained index growth toward the 2,000-point target. The rotation from speculative plays to traditional sectors like banking may indicate a healthier, more sustainable advance that could attract more stable capital flows.

high.title: Banks expected to have tens of thousands of billions more VND for lending?
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking feedback on draft amendments to Circular 22/2019 regarding safety limits and ratios for banking operations. The key change allows banks to exclude only 80% of State Treasury term deposits from total deposits when calculating the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR), meaning 20% will now be included in the denominator. This modification could significantly ease lending capacity constraints, particularly benefiting state-owned commercial banks that hold the majority of Treasury deposits. Experts suggest this could reduce pressure on retail deposit mobilization and potentially cool deposit interest rates as banks won't need to "chase" higher input rates to balance credit growth. This regulatory adjustment represents a meaningful monetary policy easing that could boost banking sector lending capacity and support economic growth while maintaining prudential oversight.

high.title: Bad debt of many banks increases sharply: Two banks have bad debt balances exceeding 40,000 billion VND
high.summary: According to financial reports from 27 listed banks, total bad debt reached 292,160 billion VND as of March 31, 2026, increasing by 28,065 billion VND compared to end-2025 (up 11%). Only three banks (VietinBank, NamABank, and ABBank) recorded declining bad debt. BIDV leads with 42,655 billion VND in bad debt, up 7,678 billion VND (22% increase) - the largest absolute increase. Sacombank follows with 41,498 billion VND, while VPBank reached 37,284 billion VND (up 18%). This deterioration in asset quality across the banking sector raises concerns about credit risk management and could impact future provisioning costs, potentially affecting bank profitability and dividend capacity. For bond investors, this trend suggests potential pressure on banking sector credit ratings and could influence SBV's monetary policy stance regarding credit growth targets.

high.title: Holding over 99% of Treasury deposits, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and Agribank benefit most from new State Bank regulations
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam officially implemented Circular 08 on May 15, 2026, amending LDR calculation methodology. The Big4 banks (Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, Agribank) will benefit most as they hold nearly 100% of Treasury deposits in the banking system. As of March 2026, Treasury deposits reached 636,000 billion VND, with the new regulation allowing 20% (approximately 127,200 billion VND) to be included in total mobilized funds for LDR calculations. This technical adjustment provides significant lending headroom for state banks without creating excessive pressure on funding costs, potentially enabling additional credit growth while maintaining prudential ratios. The move represents indirect monetary stimulus favoring state-owned banks and could influence competitive dynamics in the lending market.

medium.title: Bill Gates Foundation sells all Microsoft shares but continues pouring money into Vietnamese stocks
medium.summary: Gates Foundation Trust sold its remaining 7.7 million Microsoft shares worth $3.2 billion in Q1 2026 for charitable purposes, but continues investing in Vietnamese stocks through Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL), the largest investment fund in Vietnam's stock market managed by Dragon Capital. This signals continued foreign institutional confidence in Vietnamese equities despite global portfolio adjustments.

medium.title: Agriseco names 5 companies with notably high dividend yields amid VN-Index record highs
medium.summary: Agriseco Research highlights five dividend-focused stocks (BMP, MSH, SCS, SMB, QTP) for 2026, targeting investors seeking steady income streams amid market polarization. This dividend strategy approach becomes attractive when growth stocks carry higher chase-risk premiums and reflects defensive positioning in a record-high market environment.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Securities Director names stock groups being "forgotten" amid VN-Index peaks
medium.summary: Dragon Capital's senior director identifies undervalued sectors overshadowed by Vingroup's rally, suggesting opportunities in fundamentally strong companies with attractive valuations. While continuing to increase Vingroup exposure despite 5-10x price gains over 8 years, the fund sees potential in overlooked sectors that haven't reflected their true potential.

medium.title: How has the ranking of banks with the most deposits changed after 10 years?
medium.summary: The deposit landscape has shifted dramatically since 2015, with BIDV overtaking Agribank as the deposit king in 2024. BIDV reached over 1.95 trillion VND in deposits versus Agribank's 1.91 trillion VND, reflecting the impact of digitalization and urbanization on traditional banking hierarchies. This shift indicates changing competitive dynamics in the banking sector and deposit mobilization strategies.
